claims.statement: For every u>r and gamma>beta, the variation distance between P(H_T>u, Y_T in .) and e^{-beta(u-r)}{Q_T(.-u)+K_T} is at most (a beta/(gamma-beta)+lambda T) e^{T psi(gamma)-gamma(u-r)}, uniformly over all Borel endpoint sets.

Given H_T>u, the marked path is within 2e^{beta b}R_gamma/D_T in total variation of an explicit sampler: first-reset mark with weights lambda A(s)/D_T and A(T)/D_T, maximum-tilted pre-reset path, independent Exp(beta) overshoot.
Quantitative bounds for the overshoot, first-reset mark and fixed terminal thresholds; E[H_T-u | H_T>u] -> 1/beta for every input; J1 path limit on the scale of u.

For driftless Brownian motion C_T = e^{beta r}[Phi(sqrt(2 lambda T)) + lambda int_0^T Phi(sqrt(2 lambda s)) p_{T-s}(0) ds]; both bounds of Debicki-Hashorva-Michna Remark 3 are strict; C_1 = 1.3285764327711... at lambda=T=1, r=0.
D_T = a(1 + beta E^(beta) M_T); a standard fluctuation-theoretic consequence.
For xi_t = dt - S_t the decomposition is exact when u - r >= dT.

With i.i.d. reset positions of law rho and m(gamma)<inf for some gamma>beta, the leading measure is m(beta)e^{-beta u}{Q_T(.-u)+K^rho_T}; explicit path sampler (initial reset position tilted by e^{beta z}, mark law unchanged) and mark bounds.
Closed form vs quadrature, floating-point reflection brackets and exact-sampling Monte Carlo agree with the theory.
